walkthroughs.body_html:
Human Systems & Resource Use — a core area of Environmental Science.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Human Systems & Resource Use brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Human Systems & Resource Use.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: The ecological footprint concept was introduced by Wackernagel and Rees in:

options: Maximum population
Date annual biocapacity is exhausted
Carbon budget midpoint
Birthday of Earth Day

mcqs.q: Roughly what proportion of energy passes from one trophic level to the next?
options: Because plants only use carbon.
About 50 percent.
About 10 percent.
100 percent (everything transfers).

mcqs.q: Why is atmospheric nitrogen unavailable to most plants directly?
options: Because plants only use carbon.
Because plants cannot reach high enough to access it.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
N2 has a strong triple bond that most organisms cannot break.

mcqs.q: How does fertiliser runoff cause aquatic dead zones?
options: Excess nutrients fuel algal blooms; when algae die, decomposition depletes water oxygen.
Because plants only use carbon.
Fertiliser makes the water too acidic.
Fertiliser directly poisons fish.
